issues.display_title: Issue #897: fix(editor): a room's name in the object list is its size rank, so a new room renames it (#876)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-897-stable-room-numbers.mp4

Split out of #876, on the ruling in #896. The report's recording shows two things happening when a third room is drawn — a type appearing on a room nobody typed, and Room 42 becoming Room 43. This is the second one. It reproduces on demand; the first does not, and stays with #896.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repro

Any project. Measured against current development, on a duplicate of the demo project:

  1. Draw a room in open ground and mark it Closed. The list calls it Room 2.
  2. Draw a second room, bigger, nowhere near the first.
  3. The first room — untouched, still Closed — is now Room 3.
  4. Reload. It is still Room 3: the new label is what was stored, not a redraw glitch.

Measured on a 67-room plan (a copy of the project in #876), drawing four rooms in open ground:

A closed  rooms=68 closed=67   Room 2/Closed
drew B    rooms=69 closed=67   Room 2/Closed
drew C    rooms=71 closed=67   Room 3/Closed
drew D    rooms=72 closed=67   Room 4/Closed
reloaded  rooms=72 closed=67   Room 4/Closed

The Closed tally never moves and the room keeps its type throughout — only its name climbs. That is the whole defect, and it is why this is a separate task from #896.

What actually happens

// src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:186,192
let roomN = 0;
... { type: "room", name: r.name, typeIndex: ++roomN, engineIndex: r.i, ... }

typeIndex is the room's position in ctx.rooms. recomputeRooms fills that list with detectRooms output verbatim (model-sync.ts:93), and detectRooms returns faces sorted by area, largest first:

// src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/rooms.ts:410
.sort((p, q) => q.area - p.area);

A room with no name of its own renders as Room ${typeIndex} — so its label is a size rank, not a name. Draw a bigger room anywhere on the floor and every room smaller than it is renumbered. Delete one and they renumber back.

Room heights are the counter-example that shows the shape of the fix: they are keyed by roomKey(cx, cy) (rooms.ts:36) and survive every recompute untouched. Names have no such key.

Why it matters

  • A user who says "check Room 42" is naming something that will not be Room 42 after the next room is drawn.
  • The label is what a screenshot, a comment, and a support ticket all carry.
  • The same rank drives Area N numbering (areaN), so Areas move for the same reason.

Scope

A name needs an identity, and the codebase already has two to choose from:

  1. Number by createdAt, not by area. buildEditorObjects already reads createdAt off the stored area, and the list is already ordered by it. Ranking the fallback name the same way makes the number stable for as long as no room is deleted — a room drawn later never renumbers one drawn earlier. Smallest change; the number still shifts when a room is deleted.
  2. Persist the number. Give each detected room a nameIndex in the store alongside its id, allocated once at creation and never reused. Stable through deletes as well, and it is the only option that makes the label a real identity. Costs a store field and a migration for existing projects.

roomKey(cx, cy) is NOT a candidate on its own — it moves when a room is reshaped, which is exactly what a name must not do.

Needs a ruling

  1. Which of the two. (1) is a few lines and fixes the reported gesture; (2) is what makes the name mean something permanently. If (1), write down that a delete still renumbers.
  2. What happens to plans already saved. Every existing project's room names are area ranks today. Switching to a creation order renumbers all of them ONCE, on the next load. That is a visible, one-time change to every project — acceptable, or does it need the numbers frozen as they are?
  3. Areas too, or rooms only. areaN has the same defect through the same loop. Manual Areas are keyed by their own id, so their number could be made stable more cheaply than a Room's.

Tests

Extend src/lib/editor/__tests__/room-row-identity.test.ts — it already builds rooms through the real engine and the real bridge, which is where the numbering comes from.

  1. A bigger room does not rename a smaller one. Three squares; note the smallest room's label; draw a fourth larger than all of them; assert the label is unchanged. Today it climbs by one.
  2. The type rides with the room, not the label. Same setup, the smallest marked Closed: after the insert the row that is Closed is still the same room. (Passes today — it is the fence that keeps this task from re-opening #896.)
  3. A room drawn smaller than everything gets the next number, not a reused one.
  4. Deleting a room. Assert whatever ruling 1 decides — either the survivors keep their numbers, or the test records that they do not.
  5. Areas follow the same rule as Rooms, per ruling 3.
  6. Reload is not a renumber. Round-trip through modelToLevel / levelToModel and assert every label is what it was before.

RESULT

Commit: 46cb286 — branch feature/897-stable-room-numbering, cut from development. tsc, eslint and 2083 tests / 221 files green.

The rulings, as taken

  1. Numbering by createdAt, not a persisted counter. The store already stamps it and the list already sorts on it. A persisted nameIndex was not taken; the cost of not taking it is item 2 under "Known costs".
  2. Legacy plans renumber once, and are accepted. They already renumber on every draw today, so a single change on first save is not a new kind of instability.
  3. Areas follow the same rule, through the same helper. In practice it is close to a no-op: finishArea writes a literal Area N as a real name (commands.ts:326), so an Area's fallback number is only reached by an import with an empty name.

What changed

  • objectRows.ts — numberByAge() assigns numbers oldest-first. roomLabelsByEngineIndex(areas, rooms) is the single derivation every surface reads.
  • EngineRoomList.tsx, FloorplanEditor.tsx — both consume that helper. It takes layout.areas, not the whole level, because a Map-tab placement drag allocates a fresh level object every mousemove (#675) and a full buildEditorObjects was measured at 2.2–5.1 ms per call on 100–1200 areas, three call sites deep.
  • areaLabel.ts → pushedRoomLabel(); context.ts, editor/index.ts — the engine is handed its labels via setRoomLabels, because createdAt never enters the engine model. The two closed-room refusals read them, so the guard and the panel cannot drift (#767). With nothing pushed it falls back to the room's own name, then "this room" — a guard inventing a different number is worse than one using none.

Ties are the common case, and they no longer follow area

One Date.now() is stamped per write, so two rooms closed by a single wall stroke share a value; and the Go backend backfills a missing createdAt to the literal 1 (shared/createdat.go:33), so every legacy and Mappedin-imported floor is one tie group. Breaking those ties on ctx.rooms order would have been breaking them on the area rank — this bug, one level down: growing one room past another renumbered a room nobody touched (reproduced, then fixed). They break on the stored area's id, which rides with the room through pairByGeometry.

Consequence, stated plainly: on such a floor the numbers are not creation order. They are an arbitrary but stable order, and they change once on the first save. What is fixed there is the renumbering, not the numbers.

Known costs, pinned by tests rather than left to be found

  1. A delete closes the gap. The rank is dense, so removing a room moves every room created after it down one. Surviving a delete needs a persisted number — ruling 1, option 2, not taken.
  2. Undo after opening a room's walls gives the restored room the newest number. Undo restores the ENGINE model; it does not restore the store's area identities, which modelToLevel re-derives against the post-delete level, so the room pairs with nothing and takes a fresh id and stamp. Not introduced here — the same lost identity already sent a restored room to the top of the newest-first list — but the number now moves with it. Follow-up: give pushUndo a snapshot of layout.areas' ids and stamps, which would fix this and item 1's undo case together.

Tests

src/lib/editor/__tests__/room-number-stability.test.ts — 10 cases through the real engine and the real bridge, clock stepped by hand so createdAt is deterministic. The fixture draws rooms smallest first, so creation order is the exact reverse of area order and every assertion actually chooses between the two.

Mutation-tested rather than assumed: flipping the sort direction, dropping the id tie-break, sorting unstamped rooms last, and pinning the Area number to a constant each fail a specific test. click-cycle.test.ts gains a case proving the engine invents no number when the host pushed none.

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/897/video-897-stable-room-numbers.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 2 min 50 s. Before/after on two dev servers, same gestures, one duplicate project per build. Before: Room 2 → Room 3. After: Room 8 → Room 8.

issues.display_title: Issue #896: fix(editor): a new room wears the type of the room it displaced (#876)
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation task for bug #876. The report is a screen recording with no text; the repro below is read frame by frame off that video.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Status: the reported symptom has NOT been reproduced. An earlier revision of this issue named a root cause with confidence. That was wrong, and the correction is written out under "What was measured" — it is kept rather than deleted so nobody re-walks the same dead end. The renumbering half of the recording DID reproduce and is now #897.

Repro (from the recording)

Project Kuwait (Sample), floor Main 2, /editor/ea57d61d-2e19-48d4-bb9a-000f71f16cd4.

  1. t=7s — object count All 305. Draw a room in open ground. 305 → 310; the new row reads Room 41 / Room.

  2. t=17s — draw a second room. 310 → 315; new row Room 42 / Room. Select Room 41, set its type to Closed.

  3. t=28s — draw a third room. 315 → 320:

    Room 22   Closed     <- the room just drawn. Nobody set this.
Wall 233 232 231 230
Room 43   Room       <- this was "Room 42 / Room" one frame ago

The renumbering (Room 42 → Room 43) is #897. What is left here is the type on Room 22.

What was measured

Against a duplicate of the project in the report, on development, driving the real editor — draw a room in open ground, mark it Closed, then draw three more of varying size:

baseline  rooms=67 closed=66
drew A    rooms=68 closed=66   Room 2/Room
A closed  rooms=68 closed=67   Room 2/Closed
drew B    rooms=69 closed=67   Room 2/Closed
drew C    rooms=71 closed=67   Room 3/Closed
drew D    rooms=72 closed=67   Room 4/Closed
reloaded  rooms=72 closed=67   Room 4/Closed

The Closed tally never moves, and the room keeps its type. Only the label climbs. The same run against the candidate fix below is byte-identical, which is how the fix was found not to be one.

The mechanism that was proposed, and why it is not this

// src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:179,189
const areaByEngineIndex = new Map((level?.layout.areas ?? []).map((a, i) => [i, a]));
const stored = areaByEngineIndex.get(r.i);

r.i is the LIVE ctx.rooms position; level.layout.areas is the STORE's snapshot. detectRooms sorts faces largest-first (rooms.ts:410), so a room drawn into the middle of that order slides every smaller room one seat along, and the two index spaces disagree until the store catches up. Feed the panel the new rooms against the old level and the reported symptom appears exactly — it is unit-reproducible (room-row-identity.test.ts, 4 of 6 cases fail without the change).

It does not happen in the running app. finishWall calls recomputeRooms and then notifyChange in the same commit (interaction-tools.ts), and on.change writes the store synchronously — no debounce (FloorplanEditor.tsx:419-441). Both stores land in the same render, so there is no window in which the panel holds one and not the other. The inconsistency is real in the code and unreachable through the UI.

A candidate fix carrying the type on RoomSummary instead — read inside recomputeRooms, so the index and the meta are the same generation — is committed on feature/876-room-type-reset (cb7df36) with those tests, tsc/eslint/2078 tests green. It changes nothing about the reported symptom and is held pending ruling 1.

Still open: where does the type on Room 22 come from

The engine's own areaMeta is correct throughout — rekeyDetectedMeta (#864) moves each entry onto its new index by geometry. So a wrong type has to be introduced where areaMeta is read back into the store. The unexamined seam is the positional fallback in modelToLevel:

// src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:344-364
let at = pairedAt[i];
if (at < 0) {                                   // a room geometry recognises nothing
  while (spare < prevDetectedAreas.length && claimed.has(spare)) spare++;
  at = spare < prevDetectedAreas.length ? spare++ : -1;
}
let id = at >= 0 ? prevDetectedAreas[at].id : nanoid();
const pa = prevAreaById.get(id);
...
...metaOf(detectedMetaKey(rawIndex), pa),       // ungated: falls back to pa.type

A newly drawn room pairs with nothing, so it takes the first UNCLAIMED previous area's id — and with it pa, whose type metaOf falls back to whenever areaMeta has no entry under that key. recomputeRooms seeds every index, so the key should always be present; the question is which path reaches modelToLevel with a model that was never seeded. Two candidates, neither tested: a notifyChange that follows a mutation without a recomputeRooms, and a model restored from a history snapshot.

Worth knowing while chasing it: the plan in the recording has 66 of its 67 rooms already Closed, so almost any id a new room inherits carries closed.

Needs a ruling

  1. Does cb7df36 ship? It closes a real inconsistency and buys the test file, but it does not fix #876 and it widens RoomSummary. Land it as its own hardening change, or drop it and keep only the tests.
  2. How much further to chase this. The next step is instrumenting areaMeta and layout.areas live in the page across the recording's exact gestures, on a copy of that project. That is the only way to catch the seam; it is also an afternoon.
  3. Whether the report needs the reporter. The gestures in the recording were reproduced as read; something about the plan's state at that moment is not in the frames. One question to the reporter — was the third room drawn touching existing walls — would narrow it more than any amount of code reading.

Verified while working #897 — two mechanisms that fit this report better than the one above

Both found by probing, not by reading, and both produce "a room shows a type nobody gave it" permanently, which is what the recording shows and what the stale-render theory could not explain.

1. A Mappedin import is index-sheared from the moment it loads, on every row

src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:466 writes layout.areas in export file order, with no createdAt and no manual flag, and nothing rewrites that array until the user's first edit fires modelToLevel. Meanwhile ctx.rooms is detectRooms output, area-descending. So areaByEngineIndex.get(r.i) (objectRows.ts:207) reads a different area than the row's own room.

Driven through the real importer on samples/1fcf6c9439afd4ed10e6ce1872d7b806a445290d.zip:

stored areas as written:  Restroom, Restroom, Room 1, Room 2, Hallway 1, Hallway 2
rows before any edit:     6 / 6 sheared   (every row reads another room's stored area)
rows after drawing one room: 0 / 6 sheared   (the first modelToLevel heals it)

Isolated, a Room row rendered the manual Area's hallway type while its own said something else. On a plan where most rooms are Closed — the plan in this report is 66 of 67 — a sheared row reading closed is exactly the reported symptom.

2. Opening edits change the detected face set without recomputing ctx.rooms

detectRooms consumes doors and windows as graph edges (rooms.ts:124-125), and rebuild is only redraw2D + scene.build — it does not recompute rooms. These paths call notifyChange (so modelToLevel re-detects) with no recomputeRooms:

  • commands.ts:33 — delete door/window
  • interaction-tools.ts:43 — add door/window
  • commands.ts:360 — paste openings
  • commands.ts:370 — align openings on wall
  • model-sync.ts:180-198 — opening width

When the opening sits in a wall gap, layout.areas gains or loses an entry while ctx.rooms stays as it was, and the two lists disagree until something else recomputes.

Neither of these is touched by #897 or by cb7df36. Ruling 2 of this issue — how far to chase — now has two concrete places to start, and both are cheaper to test than instrumenting the recording's gestures.

RESULT — mechanism found, and it is neither of the two guesses above

Commit 15de1c1 on feature/896-room-type-identity, cut from development at dd191a3. Verified green with exit codes checked, not tails: tsc=0, eslint=0, vitest=0 — 222 files / 2088 tests.

The mechanism

model.areaMeta is keyed by position in detectRooms output. modelToLevel runs its own detectRooms(model) and reads the meta back by the index of THAT run (bridge.ts:336-380). And detectRooms walks doors and windows as graph edges (rooms.ts:124-125, alongAWall), so the door standing in a wall gap is what closes that ring — the shape every import produces.

Five paths handed the store a model without recomputing rooms first, so the two runs disagreed and every type slid one seat:

[1] walls only, gap open      -> 0 rooms
[1] door added, NO recompute  -> 1 room
[1] door deleted, NO recompute-> 0 rooms

Measured end to end — room A with a doorway, room B marked Closed, room C never typed:

before                       90000:-      40000:closed   19600:-
delete the doorway's door                 40000:-        19600:closed

B lost its type; C, which nobody touched, gained it.

Why it persists. The next in-session recomputeRooms re-keys by geometry and it looks right again — but the sheared level already went to setCanvasData and was autosaved, and levelToModel re-seeds areaMeta from those stored types on the next load. So the wrong room's Closed becomes its own, permanently:

RELOAD from the bad level -> 40000:-   19600:closed
one more edit after that  -> 40000:-   19600:closed

That is the "it persists, it does not heal" in the recording — and it is exactly why plain draw gestures never reproduced it. The shear needs an opening edit; the permanence needs the save and reload.

The fix

commitRooms(ctx) = recompute then notify. Every path that can change the face set goes through it: delete openings (commands.ts), paste, align, add (interaction-tools.ts), and the end of a width drag — never per tick, which would be a detectRooms per pointermove.

  • setAreaType keeps its deliberate no-recompute (it must not clear ctx.selRooms mid-click) except when its Closed sweep actually deleted an opening. There it recomputes and puts the selection back on the same room, found by the point guaranteed inside it, since the index may have moved.
  • flipType stays as it was, and now says why: it moves a record between model.doors and model.windows without touching its endpoints, and both are the same kind of edge.

One behaviour change, from the existing policy

rekeyDetectedMeta drops a type it cannot pair rather than transplanting it (#864/#798: "a missing type is visible and re-settable, a misplaced one is invisible and wrong"). So closing a doorway that merges two rooms now clears the merged room's type instead of leaving it on a neighbour. That is a consequence of recomputing at all, not a new choice.

Tests

src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/opening-face-shear.test.ts — 5 cases through the real engine and the real bridge, keyed by room AREA so a reordering cannot move an assertion onto another room. Regressed to prove they grade it: with commitRooms reduced to the old rebuild + notifyChange, 3 of 5 fail.

Also fixed here

4bd1430 — react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization was failing on development. The useMemo I added in #897 takes the rooms prop array as a dependency, which the React Compiler cannot prove is not mutated later, so it skipped optimizing EngineRoomList entirely. It shipped because that gate piped pnpm lint into tail and read the exit code of the last command in the chain rather than lint's.

Still open, and split out

#902 — an imported plan's rooms read each other's stored type until the first edit. Verified through the real importer on samples/1fcf6c9439afd4ed10e6ce1872d7b806a445290d.zip: 6 of 6 rows sheared before any edit, healed by the first modelToLevel. Same symptom, different producer, different fix — it needs no edit at all, and it hits four consumers (rows, labels, closed-room colour/logo, the toolbar's selArea).

The coupling itself stays fragile. areaMeta's numeric keys are positional over a detectRooms run that modelToLevel then re-runs independently. This closes the five known divergences; any future notifyChange-without-recompute site re-opens the same hole. A keyed-by-identity areaMeta is the standing follow-up.

issues.display_title: Issue #902: fix(editor): an imported plan's rooms read each other's type until the first edit (#876)
issues.main_description_html:
Split out of #896. Found while hunting the mechanism behind #876; it is a second, independent way for a room to show a type nobody gave it, and it needs a different fix.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

buildEditorObjects addresses the store's area list by the LIVE engine room index:

// src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:207,215
const areaByEngineIndex = new Map((level?.layout.areas ?? []).map((a, i) => [i, a]));
...
const stored = areaByEngineIndex.get(r.i);

That only holds while layout.areas is in detectRooms order. modelToLevel writes it that way (bridge.ts:386, [...detectedAreas, ...manualAreas]), but an imported level has never been through modelToLevel: src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:466 pushes each AreaLayer in export-file order, with no createdAt and no manual flag, and nothing rewrites the array until the user's first edit.

Measured, through the real importer on samples/1fcf6c9439afd4ed10e6ce1872d7b806a445290d.zip:

stored areas as the importer wrote them:
  Restroom, Restroom, Room 1, Room 2, Hallway 1, Hallway 2
rows before any edit:        6 / 6 sheared   (every row reads another room's stored area)
rows after drawing one room: 0 / 6 sheared   (the first modelToLevel heals it)

Isolated to two rooms, a small closed one written first and a big hallway one second — the labels swap completely:

import order:  [{ area: 90000, reads: "closed" }, { area: 10000, reads: "hallway" }]
after sync:    [{ area: 90000, reads: "hallway" }, { area: 10000, reads: "closed" }]

So on a freshly imported plan, every room's type subtitle belongs to a different room, until the user makes any edit.

Why it is not #896

#896 is the opening-edit shear: areaMeta's positional keys going one apart from the run modelToLevel does, fixed by recomputing rooms on the five opening paths. This one needs no opening and no edit at all — it is there from the moment an import is opened, and it is the store's array that is out of order, not the engine's keys.

The blast radius is four consumers, not one

commands.ts:66-68 already names them:

ponytail: that index alignment between ctx.rooms and layout.areas is already load-bearing for the shell colour, the room logo and the toolbar's own selArea lookup — if it ever breaks, all four break together.

They all read layout.areas by engine room index, host-side:

consumer file:line
Object list rows (type subtitle, createdAt, infoId) src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:207
Room/Area list labels via roomLabelsByEngineIndex, same derivation
Closed-room colour + logo pushed to the engine src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:618-622
The selection toolbar's selArea src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/SelectionToolbars.tsx:89

On an imported plan all four are painting, labelling and editing the wrong room.

Scope

Two shapes, and the choice is the ruling:

  1. Resolve by identity, not position. One shared resolver — engine room index → its stored area — paired the way modelToLevel already pairs, and all four consumers read it. RoomSummary would have to carry something to pair ON: the interior point recomputeRooms already computes (r.lx, r.ly) is enough for a point-in-polygon match, taking the SMALLEST containing area so a nested room does not claim its parent. Manual Areas pair by their own id. No data is written, and it is correct even for a level that never round-trips.
  2. Normalise the level on load. After engine.loadModel, if layout.areas is not already in canonical order, write the canonical level back once. One place enforces the invariant instead of four defending against it — but it is a store write on open, so it marks the project dirty, autosaves, and broadcasts to collaborators for what the user experiences as merely opening a file.

(1) is bigger code and zero risk to data. (2) is three lines and touches every imported project the first time it is opened.

Needs a ruling

  1. Which shape. If (2), say explicitly that opening an imported project writes to it.
  2. Is the import the only producer? levelToModel also drops stored areas with fewer than 3 boundary points (bridge.ts:149), which offsets every later index the same way. Worth confirming whether any real import emits one.
  3. Order of work with #896. They are independent; #896 is merged/committed separately and does not fix this.

Tests

New src/lib/editor/__tests__/area-index-identity.test.ts:

  1. Import order. Build a level whose layout.areas is NOT in detect order — small-first, big-second, different types — run levelToModel → recomputeRooms → buildEditorObjects, and assert each row reads ITS OWN area's type. Today they are swapped; the probe is in the issue above.
  2. Heals is not enough. The same assertion must hold before any edit, not only after modelToLevel.
  3. Nested rooms. A room drawn inside another must pair with its own area, not the parent's — this is what pins "smallest containing area" if ruling 1 takes shape (1).
  4. Manual Areas pair by id, not by position, through the same insert.
  5. Closed-room colour and logo maps are built for the right rooms on an unsynced level.
  6. Regression fence. On a level that HAS been through modelToLevel, nothing changes.

RESULT

Commit 28f0527, merged to development as PR #905 (723a22e). Gate verified by exit code: tsc=0, eslint=0, vitest=0 — 223 files / 2094 tests.

Ruling 1 taken: shape (1), resolve by identity. Shape (2) — normalising the level on load — was rejected because it writes to every imported project the first time it is opened: dirty flag, autosave and a collab broadcast, for what the user experiences as opening a file. The read-side fix is also correct for a level that never round-trips at all.

storedAreasByRoom() in src/lib/editor/areaResolve.ts, read by all five sites — the object rows, the Room/Area list subtitle, the closed-room colour and logo maps pushed to the engine, and the toolbar's selArea. Manual Areas pair by id first; a detected room takes the smallest unclaimed area containing its interior point (labelPoint, not the centroid, which an L or U-shaped room puts in its own notch); anything geometry cannot place falls back to the position it used to read.

closedRoomColors / closedRoomLogos now take a list indexed by engine room, so a room with no paired area has no entry rather than borrowing its neighbour's.

Ruling 2 — the boundaries.length < 3 drop in levelToModel:149 shears the same way, and is covered by the same fix: identity pairing does not care how many areas were dropped.

Tests: src/lib/editor/__tests__/area-index-identity.test.ts, 6 cases through the real engine and the real bridge. Regressed to prove they grade it — with the resolver reduced to areas[r.i], 5 of 6 fail.

No video. The before/after needs an import that produces detected Rooms, and every sample export in samples/ arrives through the wizard as Polygons, Points and Access markers with zero Room rows — after importing 1fcf6c94….zip the object list reads Access 5 … Polygon 10 … Door 7 … Wall 44 and no rooms at all. A recording would show nothing moving on either build. The evidence is the test suite plus the measurement on the real converter in the issue above.

Note — the demo cannot be filmed, and the earlier diagnosis here was wrong

Correction. An earlier revision of this note said the wizard was turning the imported floor's areas into Polygons or dropping them, because the object list showed no Room or Area rows. That was wrong, and the measurement that showed it is worth keeping:

levels: [{ id: f_cd402b70669b463f, walls: 44, areas: 6, shapes: 10 }, ...]
engineRooms: 0     <- at 8s, 15s, 25s and 40s

The store was correct all along — 6 areas, exactly what the converter produces. The engine never received the model, so detectRooms never ran and every room-derived surface was blank. That is a separate defect, now #907: loadedLevelRef outlived the engine it described, so a rebuilt engine was never given a model, and only imports showed it because they stage canvasData before navigating to the editor. Fixed and verified in the running app: engineRooms goes 0 → 6.

With #907 in, the demo runs — and still shows nothing. Both passes complete and the room rows are there, but moved = 0 on the unfixed build. The reason is in the data:

1fcf…zip   f_cd402b70669b463f  areas=6   distinctTypes=1  :: -,-,-,-,-,-
628-hi-rise.zip  three floors  areas=85/57/38  distinctTypes=1  :: -,-,…
b7c1feb…zip      areas=36      distinctTypes=1
mall-demo-consumer.zip  areas=44  distinctTypes=1
mappedin-multi-building.zip  areas=49/44/16  distinctTypes=1

Every sample import ships its areas with no type at all. So the shear is real — the rows genuinely read each other's stored record, which is what the unit tests pin — but on these files there is nothing on screen for it to move: every room reads "Room" before the edit and "Room" after.

A film would need an export whose areas carry differing types, or a real customer project imported and then typed. Not worth manufacturing one; the evidence stays the test suite (5 of 6 fail with the resolver reduced to areas[r.i]) and the pairing measurement above.

issues.display_title: Issue #859: Fix Mobile Modal Layout Positioning and Container Inset Spacing
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

Before

video-859-before.mp4

After

video-859-after.mp4

Description:

Update CSS positioning and dynamic viewport offset for location detail popups on mobile devices to prevent top header bar overlap.

Acceptance Criteria:

  1. Adjust modal top offset / CSS safe-area inset calculations to account for the total height of top floating control bars.
  2. Ensure the modal close button ("X") remains un-obscured, fully visible, and clickable on both Mobile Safari and Mobile Chrome.
  3. Verify z-index stack hierarchy so floating header controls and modal elements do not visually collide or block user inputs.

RESULT

PreviewControls is absolute left-4 top-4 z-20 with flex-wrap. At phone width it takes two rows and its bottom edge lands at 160px. The visitor info card was pinned at a constant top-4, so it opened at 64px — under the toolbar, which outranks it (z-20 over z-10).

Measured on /preview/<id> at 390x844 against the real project:

before after
toolbar bottom 160 160
card top 64 168
toolbar controls over the card 6 0
a tap on the card's title reaches "Direction" the card

All six controls — Back to Editor, Search Area, Direction, Event, Building, Floor — painted across the card's header. A tap meant for the card's title reached the Direction button, which opens the Direction panel and clears the selection, so the card the visitor was reading disappeared.

Note on AC2. The close button was already clickable in this project: row 1 of the toolbar ends at x=208 and the X sits at x≈303, so it falls in a gap between controls. It is the card's header that was buried, not the X. AC1 and AC3 were both failing.

Note on AC1's safe-area insets. Not involved. There is no env(safe-area-inset-*) anywhere in src/, and layout.tsx exports no viewport, so without viewport-fit=cover the insets resolve to 0. The cause is the toolbar's height alone.

Fix

The panels on the left already start below a measured clearance (panelTop, #811). The card now takes the same number through a new topOffset prop, and drives its position and height cap from it:

top-(--toolbar-clear)  max-h-[calc(100%_-_var(--toolbar-clear)_-_1rem)]
xl:top-4               xl:max-h-[calc(100%_-_2rem)]

Confined to below xl on purpose. From there up the two never meet, and top-4 right-14 is the approved placement from #211, whose gap above the card once rendered as a black compositing artifact over the WebGL canvas in Chromium. A breakpoint rather than a second resize listener, because whether they collide at all is a width question — the answer #851 gave the search panel.

Fixed along the way

The height cap moved from 100dvh - var(--editor-topbar-h) - 2rem to the card's own containing block. The overlay only insets itself by the navbar when standalone, so the old cap was 48px short on the public viewer, inside an embed, and over the editor. At 1440 the card is now 868px tall instead of 816.

Verification

Measured in Chromium at 360 / 390 / 1279 / 1440: the card clears the toolbar at every width below xl, holds top: 16px and calc(100% - 32px) from xl up, and the close button hit-tests to itself throughout.

Two 390x844 60fps recordings in .playwright-mcp/demo/859/ — video-859-before.mp4 and video-859-after.mp4, the same scenario against both builds. The scenario asserts on the after run, so the recording doubles as a check.

Four unit tests cover the wiring: the measured offset reaches the element, xl:top-4 survives, the height cap is no longer expressed in 100dvh, and the default is the plain top-4 inset.

The #211 compositing artifact does not recur — the gap between toolbar and card renders the map. Verified on Chromium/Vulkan on Linux; not yet checked on iOS Safari.

Residual

The xl cut is a breakpoint, not a measurement. The toolbar measured 647px wide here; on a 1280–1400px screen with much longer building and floor names it could still reach the card and would not be pushed clear. Same residual #851 accepted when it chose lg.

Files

  • src/components/editor/preview/PreviewInfoCard.tsx — topOffset prop, --toolbar-clear, breakpoint-scoped position and height cap
  • src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx — passes the measured panelTop
  • src/components/editor/preview/__tests__/PreviewInfoCard.test.tsx — 4 new tests

issues.display_title: Issue #907: fix(editor): after a Mappedin import the canvas gets no model, so the plan has no rooms
issues.main_description_html:
Found while trying to film the #902 demo: the demo could not run, because after a Mappedin import the editor canvas gets no model at all.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repro

  1. /start → name the project → confirm location → import any Mappedin export → Continue to Editor.
  2. The object list shows the walls, shapes, doors and markers the import brought — but no Room and no Area rows, ever.

Measured in the running app, reading the store and the engine directly, at 8 s, 15 s, 25 s and 40 s after landing in the editor:

levels: [{ id: f_cd402b70669b463f, walls: 44, areas: 6, shapes: 10 }, ...]
engineRooms: 0        <- at every one of the four samples

The store is correct — 44 walls, 6 areas. The engine simply never received the model, so detectRooms never ran, ctx.rooms stayed empty, and every room-derived surface is blank: the object list's Room/Area rows, the Room and Area lists, the 3D volumes, and anything keyed on a room index.

What actually happens

loadedLevelRef records the level the engine currently holds, and the load effect skips the work when nothing changed:

// src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:537
if (!level || level === loadedLevelRef.current) return;

The engine itself is built in a separate effect (:361) with deps: [], whose cleanup destroys it — but loadedLevelRef is not cleared with it, and the load effect's deps are [canvasData, activeId, floorConfigs], with no engineReady.

So when the component remounts — React's development double-invoke is the everyday case — the sequence is:

  1. engine A created; load effect loads the model into A and sets loadedLevelRef.current = level
  2. cleanup: A destroyed, engineRef.current = null, rooms cleared — loadedLevelRef still points at the level
  3. engine B created
  4. load effect re-runs only if one of its three deps changed; if it does run, level === loadedLevelRef.current sends it straight out

Engine B never gets a model.

Why only imports. For a project opened normally, canvasData arrives from the server after mount, so the effect re-runs with a genuinely new level object and loads into B. A wizard import stages canvasData into the store before it navigates to /editor/<id>, so none of the three deps ever change again — and the canvas stays empty for good.

Scope

Two lines, and they are the same bug stated twice:

  1. Clear the ref with the engine. loadedLevelRef.current = null in the engine effect's cleanup: the ref describes what that engine is holding and must not outlive it.
  2. Make the load effect depend on engineReady, so a rebuilt engine gets a load at all.

Verified in the running app on the same import, same four samples: engineRooms goes 0 → 6, with the real names (Hallway 2, Hallway 1, Restroom, …).

Needs a ruling

  1. Does this reach production? reactStrictMode is unset, so Next's default puts the double-invoke in development only, and I have not reproduced a production remount. The underlying defect — a ref outliving the object it describes — is real either way, and every genuine remount (a route change that keeps the component, a layout swap) hits it.
  2. Test coverage. There is no test file for FloorplanEditor at all, and standing one up means canvas + three.js. The verification here is the in-app measurement above. Either accept that and record it, or fund the harness.

Tests

If ruling 2 says fund it, the smallest useful shape is a mount test with the engine module mocked to a recording double:

  1. Mount, unmount, remount with an unchanging canvasData — assert loadModel was called once per engine instance, not once in total.
  2. The normal path still loads once, not twice, when canvasData arrives after mount.
  3. An empty building still clears the canvas (#536's branch) after a remount.
